summary: Matthias de Vries was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied at Leiden University (~1837–1843). He held academic posts at the University of Groningen (1849–1853) and Leiden University (1853–1891).

Matthias von Lexer studied linguistics and other fields at the University of Graz, under Franz Bopp, Moriz Haupt, and Albrecht Weber, earning a PhD from Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held professorships at Freiburg (~1863–1868), Würzburg (1868), and Munich (1890).

Matthieu Ricard is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob, earning a doctorate, and trained under Kangyour Rinpoché and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He became a Mind and Life Institute board member (~1991).

Mattia Salvini works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, also studying under Ram Shankar Tripathi, Tsultrim Gyaltsen, and K. Srinivasan. He taught at Mahidol University (~2011).

Mauli Chand Prasad is a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics who earned his doctorate from Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna. In 1984, he was attested as Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Maurice Bloomfield was an Indologist and linguist who studied under William Dwight Whitney and Charles Rockwell Lanman, completing his PhD at Johns Hopkins University (~1878–1879). He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

Maurice Frank Wiles was a religious studies scholar who studied at Christ's College and Ridley Hall, Cambridge. He held posts at Ridley Hall, University of Ibadan, University of Cambridge, King's College London, and was Regius Professor of Divinity at Oxford (1970–1991).

Maurice Grammont was a linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1888–1892) under Ferdinand de Saussure. He later served on the faculty at the University of Montpellier from ~1905 to 1939.
Maurice Jametel was a scholar in Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes from ~1875 to 1878 and subsequently held a post there from ~1886 to 1889.

Maurice Leenhardt was a scholar of religious studies and other subjects. He studied under Marcel Mauss between ~1926 and 1930, whom he later succeeded, and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from ~1940 to 1951.
Maurice Walshe worked in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He studied under Walpola Rahula and held an academic post attested at the University of London in 2009.

Maurine Stuart was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Manitoba, under Nadia Boulanger, and with traditional teachers Hakuun Yasutani, Eido Shimano, and Soen Nakagawa. In 1979, she became president and spiritual director of Cambridge Buddhist Association.

Maurizio Taddei worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was a professor at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (~1964–1977) and Editorial Committee Director at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East.

Mauro Maggi specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctoral degree from the University of Naples "L'Orientale," served as Director of the Italian Institute for Africa and the East, and joined Sapienza University of Rome.

Mavis L. Fenn specializes in Buddhist and religious studies, completing a PhD at McMaster University under Graeme MacQueen. She served as Assistant Professor at United College (attested 2005–2006) and Professor and Department Chair at the University of Waterloo (attested 2016).

Max Deeg is an Indologist, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Würzburg. He served as Head of School at Cardiff University (attested 2010–2021) and Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Max Kaltenmark was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He directed the Centre Franco-Chinois d'Études sinologiques de Pékin (1946) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1949–1953), holding later posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris.

Max Leopold Margolis was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who earned a Ph.D. from Columbia University (1891). He held positions at Hebrew Union College, the University of California, Berkeley, and Dropsie College for Hebrew and Cognate Learning (1909–1932).
Max Lindenau was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig University until 1913 under Ernst Windisch.

Max Oidtmann is a scholar in Tibetology, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard under Mark Elliott, later holding posts at Georgetown University, Georgetown University in Qatar, and the University of Munich.
